rules.rule: the last line is the last line
rules.evil: The cursor can rest on the empty line after a file's final newline: G, 5j, w, }, dd, dk, dG, L and gj go there, and so does M in a short buffer. j from the last line goes there without an error; only j, gj and C-d on that empty line fail.
rules.die_vim: What your Evil does when the text has no final newline, with the newline kept: the cursor never rests on the empty line after it. Motions stop on the last line. j, gj, + and C-d on the last line fail, and so do w and e on its last character and } at its end; a macro ends at the first failure. dj, cj and yj on the last line act on that line, as Evil's do (Vim's fail). After dd, dk or dG removes the last lines, the cursor goes to the new last line, in the column the delete started in (S5 row 2). G recentres on the last line, and H, M and L clamp to it.

rules.rule: a count before / or ? finds the nth match
rules.die_vim: As in Vim: 2/x goes to the second match after the cursor, wrapping past the end as one search does. A later n moves one match.

rules.rule: an empty search repeats the last one
rules.die_vim: As in Vim: / or ? with an empty pattern searches for the last pattern again, in its own direction. With no last pattern it's an error.

rules.rule: . inside a macro repeats the macro's change
rules.evil: . signals an error inside a macro, since Evil runs macros without command hooks.
rules.die_vim: As in Vim: a change made inside a macro becomes the last change, so a later . in the same macro repeats it.

rules.rule: a linewise put over the last line keeps the final newline
rules.evil: Vp (and VP, and Vjp over the last two lines) on the buffer's last line leaves an empty line and drops the final newline.
rules.die_vim: As in Vim: the lines are replaced and the final newline stays.

rules.rule: a count before H counts from 1
rules.evil: nH goes to line n+1 of the window: 3H goes to the fourth line.
rules.die_vim: As in Vim: nH goes to line n of the window, so 3H goes to the third. H, M and L otherwise follow Evil (S5 row 20).

rules.rule: undo is Vim's u and C-r
rules.evil: Your Evil has no redo (evil-undo-system is unset): C-r signals an error, and u after another command redoes, as Emacs's undo chain does.
rules.die_vim: Your S5 answer: u steps back and C-r steps forward, as in Vim (scope §10). C-r with nothing to redo fails, as u with nothing to undo does.

DIE's regex syntax is Rust's (D4): the same change is :s/(foo) (bar)/$2 $1/, with the same result. The replacement expands $N and ${N} as the regex crate does, so a group followed by a letter or digit needs braces: ${1}x.

rules.evil: In emacs-lisp-mode and python-mode, a new line is indented by the language.
rules.die_vim: Until file-type modes (M1) give die-vim a language's indentation, a new line is indented like the line above, as Evil does in text.
